title: Shanidar A Neanderthal killed by a spear

caption:
A Neanderthal who died 75,000 years ago was probably killed by a wooden spear, and the same man had once survived a face injury that someone must have helped him through.

The remains are known as Shanidar A, found in Shanidar Cave in Iraqi Kurdistan. A 15 mm round hole in his left shoulder blade matches the shape of a wooden spear. Researchers at the University of Cambridge think the spear entered the front of his left chest, passed through a lung and major blood vessels, and came out through the shoulder blade. Death would have been quick. It may have been a deliberate shot at the heart, though an accidental hunting injury cannot be ruled out.

Years earlier he had suffered a different injury: a lower front tooth was split and the teeth beside it were pushed inward. Tartar built up on the broken tooth, which suggests he lived at least another year. The team thinks other Neanderthals may have fed him soft food while he healed. He was about 45 when he died.

His body was found under roughly 7.5 to 8 metres of rock and sediment, at the bottom of a small cluster of five Neanderthal burials, with a large upright boulder as a marker. The researchers call this "intentional and symbolic funerary behavior".

Would you want to know how your ancestors lived, even if it was violent?

Source: ScienceDaily (University of Cambridge), Scientific Reports
